- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/1.00 spikes followed by 0.00/0.33 corrections, model tends to “stick” to high forecasts; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment after 3 consecutive bullish sentiment days.
